81281.subject: Stock-Token Loans Face Their First Weekend
81281.body:
**gm, Defiers!**

These are the biggest stories in DeFi and crypto:

* **[Aero](https://thedefiant.io/news/defi/aero-launches-aerodrome-velodrome-merge-seven-chains)**[ merged Aerodrome and Velodrome on 7 chains](https://thedefiant.io/news/defi/aero-launches-aerodrome-velodrome-merge-seven-chains)

* **[Starknet](https://thedefiant.io/news/blockchains/starknet-poll-backs-post-quantum-layer-1-research-with-93-52-support)**[ poll: 93.52% back L1 research](https://thedefiant.io/news/blockchains/starknet-poll-backs-post-quantum-layer-1-research-with-93-52-support)

* **[Visa](https://thedefiant.io/converge/infrastructure/visa-in-talks-to-buy-fireblocks-for-about-2-5-billion-axios)**[ in talks to buy Fireblocks for $2.5B](https://thedefiant.io/converge/infrastructure/visa-in-talks-to-buy-fireblocks-for-about-2-5-billion-axios)

* **[Ethereum](https://thedefiant.io/news/blockchains/ethereum-developers-cancel-oct-26-glamsterdam-upgrade-on-hoodi)**[ devs cancel Glamsterdam on Hoodi](https://thedefiant.io/news/blockchains/ethereum-developers-cancel-oct-26-glamsterdam-upgrade-on-hoodi)

* **[Morpho](https://thedefiant.io/news/defi/morpho-opens-robinhood-stock-tokens-to-stablecoin-borrowing)**[ opens loans on Robinhood Stock Tokens](https://thedefiant.io/news/defi/morpho-opens-robinhood-stock-tokens-to-stablecoin-borrowing)

Tokenized stocks are breaking free from exchange accounts and moving into DeFi lending markets. Today Morpho [opened Robinhood Stock Tokens to stablecoin borrowing](https://thedefiant.io/news/defi/morpho-opens-robinhood-stock-tokens-to-stablecoin-borrowing), and Kraken said it [now lists more than 1,000 xStocks](https://thedefiant.io/news/cefi/kraken-says-its-xstocks-lineup-now-exceeds-1-000). Yesterday, Pendle [added leveraged loops on Coinbase stock tokens on Base](https://thedefiant.io/news/defi/pendle-expands-one-click-looping-to-yield-assets-and-tokenized-stocks). A holder can now borrow dollars against Nvidia exposure without selling it. 

So, what happens to that loan when the stock market closes?

A lending market must price its collateral at all times. Robinhood [advertises 24/7 trading](https://thedefiant.io/news/tradfi-and-fintech/robinhood-vs-securitize-stock-token-access-compared) for its onchain Stock Tokens. Its Chainlink price feeds update 24 hours a day, five days a week. Aave Labs says its equity feeds hold the last price over weekends and U.S. holidays. Interest on the loan accrues during that time, and the collateral price stays fixed. (Paboxo, another lender on Robinhood Chain, pauses liquidations while the stock market is closed). LlamaRisk, a DeFi risk firm, warns that the first new price can include the whole weekend's move. A loan that was healthy on Friday can be liquidatable at that update.

# Thursday links: These links may or may not be safe to click on

[Harari on our bovine financial future](https://www.ceskatelevize.cz/porady/10441294653-hyde-park-civilizace/9271-english-versions/47309?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

The good news is that Yuval Noah Harari does not think AI poses a Terminator-style risk. No robots are coming to exterminate us.

The bad news is that the peaceful outcome he foresees instead is not much more appealing: “We are the cows of the future,” he told an interviewer this week.

He means that metaphorically: The world AI is now creating will soon be as incomprehensible to us as the human world is to cows.

The historian-turned-futurist explains that humans “took over the planet” by building “bureaucracies.” Our lives, he says, are shaped by the bureaucracies of banks, governments, legal systems, and religious institutions. 

Animals’ lives, too. The number of cows that exist, how they exist, and where, is a function of the money, markets, laws, and religions humans have invented; none of which they understand.

“How do you explain the bond market to cows,” Harari asks, “even though it controls their lives?”

We could soon find ourselves in the same situation. For the same reason. The bureaucracies of the future will be shaped by AI, Harari warns, because AIs are “bureaucratic natives” and will therefore be much better at building them.

81070.subject: 💰 The Funding: What happens if MSCI drops crypto treasuries like Strategy?
81070.body:
View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/c1c9af72-58d8-47c5-88eb-8e5007f7e3dc/unnamed__17_.png?t=1789144554)
Caption: 

Written by Yogita Khatri  | Edited by Zack Abrams

———————————————————————————

Presented By:

View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/0f002faa-88b1-4362-8467-fbc25a6c61ee/Screenshot_2026-10-16_at_4.02.56_PM__3___1___1___1_.png?t=1792184177)
Caption: 

———————————————————————————

----------
Happy Sunday, and welcome to the 62nd edition of [The Funding](https://www.theblock.co/newsletters/the-funding)!

MSCI [finalized rules](https://www.theblock.co/news/business/2026-10-15-msci-rules-could-exclude-strategy-mstr-from-indexes-418729) on Oct. 15 that could push Strategy and other crypto treasury companies out of its main global indexes as soon as Nov. 30. What would that mean for how these companies raise money, and is anyone still willing to fund them? I caught up with investors and analysts to find out.

Let's get into it.


----------———————————————————————————

----------
# THE INSIDE VIEW

## What if MSCI drops crypto treasuries?


----------View image: (https://media.beehiiv.com/cdn-cgi/image/fit=scale-down,format=auto,onerror=redirect,quality=80/uploads/asset/file/2012e140-bc90-4ae9-b029-9f403353161b/Dat-Image-1200x675.jpg?t=1792371900)
Caption: 

----------
Index provider MSCI recently [approved new rules](https://app2.msci.com/webapp/index_ann/DocGet?pub_key=aq0wbkjxPgo%3D&lang=en&format=html) that target "non-operating" companies, which mainly hold assets instead of running a business, such as digital asset treasury firms, or DATs.

Under the new rules, MSCI will first check whether a company has substantial operating assets, such as equipment or inventory. In the [proposal MSCI published in August](https://www.msci.com/downloads/documents/indexes/consultations/equity/Consultation%20on%20Eligibility%20of%20Non-Operating%20Companies%20for%20the%20%20MSCI%20Global%20Investable%20Market%20Indexes.pdf), that meant operating assets making up more than half of total assets. Companies that fail this check face five financial tests, which in the proposal included whether a company generates operating cash flow and how much it relies on raising capital to buy assets. Those flagged on four or more will be excluded.

Current index members get some leeway: they will be removed only if they fail in both of their two most recent annual filing periods. If they fail in only one, they stay in the index unless they fail the following year. Companies not yet in the index are blocked if they fail in either of the last two years.

In a simulation published in August using May data, MSCI flagged two bitcoin treasury companies, Michael Saylor's Strategy and Japan's Metaplanet, for potential exclusion. Ethereum treasury firm SharpLink
